metaTitle: SHB30321 Cert III Nail Technology RPL — Nail Tech
metaDescription: Working as a nail technician? Get the SHB30321 Certificate III in Nail Technology through RPL using your salon experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SHB30321 Certificate III in Nail Technology is the national qualification for nail technicians. If you already do manicures, pedicures, acrylics and nail art for clients, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without starting a course.
whoIsItFor:
• Nail technicians in salons and nail bars
  • Mobile and home-based nail technicians
  • Nail salon owners
  • Nail technicians who trained overseas

You'll usually have a year or more of regular client work: manicures and pedicures, acrylic enhancements, electric file work, nail art, advising on products and following hygiene and infection control rules.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos of your work: acrylics, nail art, manicures and pedicures
  • Client records with personal details removed
  • Certificates from product or short courses
  • A reference from the salon owner or manager, or client testimonials if you work for yourself
  • Infection control and hygiene procedures you follow
licensingInfo: There's no national licence for nail technicians, but local councils and state health rules can apply to salons, especially for hygiene and skin penetration. If you run your own salon, check your council's registration requirements.
description: The SHB30321 Certificate III in Nail Technology covers the skills of a qualified nail technician: manicures and pedicures, acrylic nail enhancements, nail art, electric file equipment, advising on beauty products and services, salon services and financial transactions, researching industry information, and safe hygiene, health and work practices including infection control.

faqs.q: Can I get a nail technology qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work regularly as a nail technician. Photos of your work, client records and references are assessed against the units, and practical services are observed or recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to be a nail technician?
faqs.a: There's no national licence, but local councils may require salons to be registered and to meet hygiene rules. Check with your council if you run your own business.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: Do my short nail courses count?
faqs.a: They help, especially alongside photos and records showing you use those skills with clients.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SHB40121 Cert IV in Beauty Therapy RPL — Fast Track
metaDescription: Working as a beauty therapist? Get the SHB40121 Certificate IV in Beauty Therapy through RPL using your salon experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SHB40121 Certificate IV in Beauty Therapy is the core qualification for beauty therapists. If you already do facials, waxing, lash and brow treatments, make-up, massage and nails, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without starting a course.
whoIsItFor:
• Beauty therapists in salons, day spas and resorts
  • Lash, brow and waxing specialists with a broad range of treatments
  • Beauty salon owners
  • Beauty therapists who trained overseas

You'll usually have a year or more delivering a broad range of treatments: facials and skin care, waxing, lash and brow services, make-up, body massage, tanning, manicures and pedicures, plus retail sales.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of treatments you've performed
  • Treatment and consultation records with client details removed
  • Certificates from product and short courses
  • Retail sales records or product recommendations
  • A reference from the salon owner or manager
licensingInfo: There's no national licence for beauty therapists, but local councils and state health rules apply to some treatments, such as waxing, skin penetration and some skin treatments. Check your council's requirements if you run your own salon.
description:
The SHB40121 Certificate IV in Beauty Therapy covers the skills of a qualified beauty therapist: facial treatments and skin care, waxing, lash and brow services, make-up design and application, body massage, cosmetic tanning, manicures and pedicures, knowledge of skin and body structures and nutrition, salon services and sales, professional standards online, and safe hygiene and work practices.

It replaces SHB40115. The next level is the SHB50121 Diploma of Beauty Therapy.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Beauty Therapy through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you deliver a broad range of beauty treatments. Photos, treatment records and a salon reference are assessed against the units, and practical treatments are observed.

faqs.q: Should I do the Certificate IV or the Diploma?
faqs.a: The Certificate IV covers core beauty treatments. If you also deliver advanced skin and body treatments, the Diploma of Beauty Therapy may suit you. We can check your experience against both.

faqs.q: I only do lashes and brows. Can I get this qualification?
faqs.a: The Certificate IV covers a wide range of treatments, so you need experience across most of them. If your work is narrower, talk to us about the best fit.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SHB50216 Diploma of Salon Management RPL — Online
metaDescription: Own or manage a salon? Get the SHB50216 Diploma of Salon Management through RPL using your experience running the business. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SHB50216 Diploma of Salon Management is the management qualification for hair, beauty and nail salons. If you already run a salon, lead the team and manage services and sales, RPL turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Salon owners and managers in hair, beauty, nails or spa
  • Senior stylists and therapists who manage staff
  • Multi-salon and franchise managers

You'll usually have a few years managing a salon: recruiting and inducting staff, leading the team, managing services and sales, marketing the business and keeping the workplace safe.
evidenceExamples:
• Recruitment, induction and staff records (with names removed)
  • Sales, service and booking reports
  • Marketing and promotion you've run
  • Salon policies, procedures and WHS records
  • A reference from the salon owner or your accountant if you own it
description: The SHB50216 Diploma of Salon Management covers running a personal services business: reviewing HR functions, managing recruitment, selection and induction, developing sustainability policies, leading teams, managing treatment services and sales, promoting the business and providing a safe work environment.

faqs.q: Can I get the Diploma of Salon Management through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you manage or own a salon. Your staff, sales and marketing records and a reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need a hairdressing or beauty qualification first?
faqs.a: No, there are no entry requirements. Experience managing a salon is what matters.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
